newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended mostly up on industry buying after lower-than-expected tenders on the first notice/tender day for the spot November contract. Front month November added a hefty $32 to close at $1,495 and widened the closely-watched November/January spread to a high of $110 from $78 at Thursday's close. However, traders said fresh robusta origin supplies are ample and poised to make their way to western markets soon. This, in their view, will put pressure on robusta prices. In New York arabica futures ended mixed in scant volume as a holiday in Europe dampened market participation. Nearby December rose 5 points to close at 117.25 cents/lb, while March added 35 points to close at 106.45 cents/lb. Outer months closed 25 points higher to 50 points lower. ICO export data for September showed decreased shipments which helped to tighten the nearby supply situation. Demand is on the rise and stocks are lower than a year ago, so the reduced exports will be felt by the market.

ICO - Coffee exports to all destinations by exporting members of the International Coffee Organization (ICO) during September totalled 4.844 million 60-kg bags down 972,340 bags from exports of 5.817 million bags in September 1995, and down 616,044 bags from exports of 5.460 million bags in August 1996. Brazil exported 1,298,682 bags in September, down from 1,543,283 bags in September 1995 and down from 1,703,114 bags in August. Colombia exported 680,354 bags in September, compared with 710,484 bags last September and 751,456 bags in August. Exports to all destinations by exporting members in the 12 months October/September 1995/96 totalled 71.706 million bags, up from 65.068 million bags the previous year.

THAILAND - According to the Commerce Ministry coffee production in 1996/97 (October/September) will reach 1.378 million 60-kg bags up from 1.264 million bags produced the previous year. Domestic consumption is expected to reach 500,000 60-kg bags, an increase of about 20 percent. According to ICO statistics consumption in 1994/95 reached 283,000 bags and rose to 417,000 bags the following year. However, the consumption figures are at odds with the production and trade figures. The Commerce Ministry has prepared 417.189 million baht as aid in payment of customs duties for Thai coffee exporters if coffee prices fall below forecasts. The Ministry recently said it would support growers if bean prices fall below 30 baht per kg.

SPAIN - Spain imported 282,207 bags of coffee in July 1997, 21 percent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 2.121 million bags, 7.8 percent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 rose by 2.2 percent to 3.225 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/July 1996 were Uganda (589,600 vs 402,100 bags), and Colombia (220,700 vs 201,900 bags). The country exported 299,800 bags of coffee in January/July 1996, 23 percent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 6.7 percent to 401,000 bags.
